Name: Bronze Skin
Effect: The first time you take damage each fight, gain 2 Harden. When it expires, your next Mace hit applies Armor Break.
Payoff: Turns incoming damage into a delayed offensive opening.

Name: Venom Mace
Effect: Mace hits against Poisoned enemies resolve one Poison tick and convert one stack into Acid.
Payoff: Poison gear becomes immediate damage and armor shred.

Name: First Bronze Age
Effect: Combo slot 1 gains +8% damage per equipped Bronze item.
Payoff: Material tags and strip position become build choices.

Name: Gut Instinct
Effect: Every 5 effective INT contributes +1 effective STR to Mace actions.
Payoff: Opens INT gear and Wizard investment to physical builds.

Name: Mighty Swing
Effect: 110% Mace finisher. Gain +35% damage per skipped or disabled slot passed before it, then reset the strip.
Payoff: Routing mutations become a deliberate wind-up.

Name: Second Bronze Age
Effect: Combo slot 2 gains one 70%-power extra hit per two equipped Bronze items.
Payoff: Bronze quantity feeds multihit and on-hit effects.

Name: Warcry
Effect: Apply Weaken and Mark for 2 turns. Your next miss against that enemy is salvaged into a normal hit.
Payoff: Creates a safe setup window for risky attacks.

Name: Mace Mastery
Effect: Bludgeon hits against Armor-Broken enemies bank +25% damage onto the next strip slot.
Payoff: Rewards sequencing Armor Break before a payoff action.

Name: Third Bronze Age
Effect: Combo slot 3 is 6% faster per Bronze item. Speed beyond 30% becomes Focus.
Payoff: Excess material synergy converts into accuracy.

Name: Pain Memory
Effect: Store 25% of post-armor damage taken. Your next Finisher adds it, capped at 20% max HP.
Payoff: Healing, armor, speed, and finisher timing share one risk window.

Name: Barbarian Rage
Effect: The next 2 actions gain damage and speed. A kill during Rage retriggers the opener.
Payoff: Aim a two-action bank at multihit, Mighty Swing, or a room reset.

Name: Living Alloy
Effect: Harden and Fortify stacks count as Bronze items. A critical may consume one stack to repeat the current slot.
Payoff: Defense, equipment, crits, and routing become one engine.

Name: Iron Discipline
Effect: Once per fight, a miss does not reset the strip; lose all Focus instead.
Payoff: Focus doubles as accuracy and combo insurance.

Name: Riposte
Effect: After taking a hit, your next Sword action gains Pierce; if armor absorbed damage, it gains +1 hit.
Payoff: Enemy attacks determine your offensive cadence.

Name: Cadence Keeper
Effect: Alternating actions above and below base speed grants Focus. Repeating a speed band removes one.
Payoff: Mixed-speed strips outperform all-fast strips.

Name: Challenge
Effect: Mark and Weaken the enemy. Strip its next damage bonus and deposit it as Fortify on you.
Payoff: Turns enemy buffs into defense.

Name: Shield Geometry
Effect: When armor reduces a hit to zero, Expose the attacker and jump to your first Sword action.
Payoff: Armor changes routing, not only effective HP.

Name: Measured Cut
Effect: 90% Sword attack. Bank damage equal to armor unused since your last turn onto the next action.
Payoff: Quiet enemy turns become an offensive resource.

Name: Commander's Opening
Effect: First normal hit lowers Combo threshold; a first-hit critical lowers Crit threshold instead.
Payoff: The opening roll selects the fight plan.

Name: Mobile Bulwark
Effect: Each Fortify stack gives the next action -3% speed, then expires.
Payoff: Choose when to cash defense into tempo.

Name: Flow State
Effect: Three different actions connect without a miss: gain one reroll and exploding dice on the next action.
Payoff: Rewards action diversity and precise sequencing.

Name: Sword Mastery
Effect: Sword hits against Exposed enemies advance two slots; against Marked enemies, advance zero.
Payoff: Status choice accelerates or holds the strip.

Name: Second Wind
Effect: Ending a combo without missing heals 8% max HP and converts leftover Focus into Fortify.
Payoff: Clean execution sustains long dungeons.

Name: Unbroken Line
Effect: Once per fight, hold a slot when the strip would reset. Reaching the Finisher from that hold retriggers the opener.
Payoff: Salvage, routing, and acceleration can form a controlled loop.

Name: Shadowcraft
Effect: Your first connected Dagger action Marks the enemy. Hitting another target moves the Mark.
Payoff: Target commitment becomes the core Rogue rule.

Name: Envenomed Edge
Effect: Dagger hits convert one Poison stack into two Bleed; critical hits convert two.
Payoff: Trade status duration for action-triggered burst.

Name: Ghost Step
Effect: After a miss, gain miss salvage and skip the next strip slot on your following connect.
Payoff: Failure can intentionally route around an awkward action.

Name: Snake Eyes
Effect: Natural 2 and 12 grant Loaded. At 2 Loaded, replace the next roll with 20.
Payoff: Exact faces create a slow probability engine.

Name: Hemorrhage
Effect: When Bleed ticks, apply Expose for one turn; if already Exposed, add Armor Break.
Payoff: Enemy speed changes the debuff payoff window.

Name: Misdirect
Effect: Low damage. On connect, replace the next strip action with the most recent action that missed.
Payoff: Failure becomes a selectable combo component.

Name: Loaded Dice
Effect: Replace the next natural roll with 6, 12, or 18 based on this action's strip slot.
Payoff: Strip placement controls deterministic trigger faces.

Name: Toxic Ledger
Effect: Each different DoT on the Mark adds +10% Finisher damage; the Finisher consumes the shortest DoT.
Payoff: Curate mixtures and durations instead of one maximum stack.

Name: Technical Debt
Effect: Distinct action tags add Debt. Repeating a tag cashes all Debt into Expose stacks.
Payoff: Players author their own setup and cash-out cycle.

Name: Dagger Mastery
Effect: Only the final multihit applies status, but it applies once per prior hit.
Payoff: Multihit count becomes a controlled status amplifier.

Name: No Witnesses
Effect: Killing a Marked enemy retriggers the opener and preserves one miss-salvage charge.
Payoff: Room sequencing and overkill become strip planning.

Name: Perfect Crime
Effect: On Marked death, copy the shortest DoT and highest debuff to the next enemy; resume after the Finisher.
Payoff: Status and routing persist as a room-to-room engine.

Name: Arcane Weave
Effect: The first elemental status each fight grants Focus and +1 temporary INT. A different element refreshes it.
Payoff: Element variety starts the Wizard engine.

Name: Kindle
Effect: Burn on a Poisoned enemy consumes one Poison to add Acid and +1 Burn.
Payoff: Cross-class Poison becomes an elemental reagent.

Name: Spell Memory
Effect: Repeating a tag adds AMP and action length. Changing tags cashes AMP onto the new action and clears both.
Payoff: Choose how long to charge repetition before pivoting.

Name: Prime Theory
Effect: Natural prime faces grant Theorem. At 3 Theorems, the next non-prime roll explodes.
Payoff: Roll history matters without removing randomness.

Name: Thermal Shock
Effect: Slow on Burning consumes both to Stun; Burn on Slowed instead adds Vulnerability.
Payoff: Element order chooses control or damage.

Name: Echo Spell
Effect: On Combo, retrigger the previous spell slot; on a normal hit, repeat the next slot instead.
Payoff: The roll band selects backward or forward routing.

Name: Rewrite Fate
Effect: Spend all Theorems. Replace the next natural roll with 5 + 5 per Theorem, capped at 20.
Payoff: Probability control becomes a visible timing resource.

Name: Catalyst
Effect: Acid armor loss becomes Burn, Poison, or Focus according to current slot modulo 3.
Payoff: Armor and strip position choose the reaction output.

Name: Channel
Effect: Bank +50% AMP and -20% speed onto the next action; if it misses, preserve half.
Payoff: A risky setup can target damage, status, or a retrigger.

Name: Dungeon Analysis
Effect: Record the prior room's common roll band. The first roll in another band next room gains advantage.
Payoff: Observed randomness informs the next room's opening.

Name: Wand Mastery
Effect: The Wand bonus slot copies opener tags and Finisher cadence bonuses.
Payoff: The extra slot becomes a programmable bridge.

Name: Grand Equation
Effect: Once per combo, natural roll + strip slot = 21 retriggers the opener with current elemental statuses.
Payoff: Roll math, strip construction, reactions, and echoes converge.
